subject: Re-test: scope acceptance and retest summary for Acme penetration remediation
messages:
From: James Porter <auditor@secureaudit.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-contacts@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: re-test scope confirmation and evidence for Acme remediations

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for coordinating the remediation window for Acme Corp. We completed the first pass of the retest on 2026-10-28 and had a handful of outstanding items where we requested additional evidence or configuration changes. Before I prepare the formal retest report, could you please confirm the final scope we should validate against and provide the following: 

- The finalized list of IPs/hostnames to be included in the external scan (so we can ensure no blind spots).
- A short remediation summary for each of the previously reported findings (what was changed, when, and the verification steps you ran).
- Any post-remediation network scans or logs you want to include in the delta appendix.

If you prefer, we can limit the retest to the 7 critical/9 high findings that were marked as remediated in your tracker, but we need explicit confirmation of which items to close versus re-open for further testing.

Target timeline: if we get scope and artifacts by EOD 2026-11-02, we can finalize the report and send a retest acceptance note by 2026-11-08.

Thanks,
James Porter
Senior Auditor, SecureAudit Inc.
attachments: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: James Porter <auditor@secureaudit.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, ops-contacts@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: re-test scope confirmation and evidence for Acme remediations

James —

Appreciate the timeline. Confirming scope below for the retest:

- External attack surface: acme-prod.example.com (54.210.12.66), acme-admin.example.com (34.82.145.11).
- Internal-facing services: no internal scans are requested — limit to externally routable services that were in the original engagement.
- Findings to validate: close-out verification for 7 critical and 9 high items (listed in the tracker); please re-open for testing only the two medium items flagged as "config drift" if you see evidence of exposure.

Attached is a concise remediation summary and the patch manifest we promised (remediation_patch_manifest.csv). Rishi also collected a fresh network scan post-patch — included as network-scan-delta.txt.

Let me know if you need additional logs (we can pull host-level audit entries for the two highest-risk changes). We agree to the timeline: scope and artifacts delivered now, please aim to issue the retest acceptance by 2026-11-08.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
attachments: remediation_patch_manifest.csv, network-scan-delta.txt

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-contacts@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-04T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: remediation summary and evidence for Acme retest (SEC-842)

Marissa / Steph —

Summary of what we changed and evidence locations (short form):

1) Critical: unauthenticated S3 list exposure — fixed by enforcing bucket policy and rotating keys (patched 2026-10-20). Evidence: remediation_patch_manifest.csv row IDs 1-3; S3 ACLs snapshot stored in drive link (see HubSpot note).
2) High: JWT signing key leakage (dev key used in prod) — rotated keys, forced token invalidation, updated KMS policy (patched 2026-10-22). Evidence: key rotation timestamped entries, audit log excerpts attached.
3) High: outdated SSH banner allowed weak ciphers — disabled weak ciphers via config push on 2026-10-25, applied centrally. Evidence: network-scan-delta.txt shows cipher list cleaned.

We ran an internal verification run (automated smoke tests + manual checks) and followed the same verification heuristics used in the original report. The delta scan captured the removal of the exposed endpoints flagged earlier.

Attached: redwood_retest_report_v2.pdf (summary of verification steps for the 16 items), remediation_patch_manifest.csv, network-scan-delta.txt. I pulled the list of host-level audit entries you may want and can send privately if the auditor asks for them.

Note: two medium items (config drift) were intentionally deferred pending Acme's confirmation on desired behavior — we flagged them as "deferred" in the tracker and included notes in the retest report.

Rishi
Lead Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_retest_report_v2.pdf, remediation_patch_manifest.csv, network-scan-delta.txt

From: James Porter <auditor@secureaudit.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-contacts@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-08T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final: re-test conclusion and retest acceptance summary for Acme Corp

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. We reviewed the retest packet (redwood_retest_report_v2.pdf) and the network delta. Based on our validation steps, SecureAudit agrees to the following: 

- Confirmed: 7 critical and 9 high findings remediated and verified.
- Deferred: the two medium "config drift" items remain open and documented as exceptions in the delta appendix; we did not re-classify them as high-critical during this retest.
- Acceptance: issuing a retest acceptance summary (attached) and a brief acceptance note we will provide to Acme for their internal compliance.

Attached: retest-acceptance-summary.txt (signed acceptance from SecureAudit). If Acme's compliance team needs a signed PDF or DocuSign flow, loop procurement@acme-corp.com and we will route it.

We consider this retest closed for the validated items. If Acme wants re-validation on the deferred items after they implement their chosen config, we can schedule a targeted follow-up.

Regards,
James Porter
Senior Auditor, SecureAudit Inc.
attachments: retest-acceptance-summary.txt
